clue.text: Skiing, and so on, in snow trip rest organized

indicators.note: the words are put into a new order, so their letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the three words supply exactly the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday-maker's snowy trip, with some rest built in.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing is one example of the cold-weather pastimes grouped under this name, and 'and so on' widens it to the class.

clue.text: Like 10 in mellow hit, evergreen

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

parts.note: the answer runs from the last letter of mellow through hit into the start of evergreen

explanation.surface: A seasonal song review: a mellow hit that has become an evergreen.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is CHRISTMAS, and the Bing Crosby song gives the phrase White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowy festive season is described by this colour word, as in the famous song title.

clue.text: Old PM on European base used by 17 Down 10

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister stationed at a European base used by Santa.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 Down 10 is Father Christmas, whose workshop is traditionally at the top of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places Santa's home and workshop at this polar point in the Arctic.

clue.text: Covers 75% of main points about legal action

indicators.note: the three points go around the legal word, enclosing it

parts.note: the four main compass points are N, E, S and W; three of the four are used
a case is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: Covering most of the key points of a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main points' are the cardinal points of the compass, and 75% of four is three.
explanation.definitionFit: To encase something is to enclose or wrap it, so the verb is a synonym of covers.

clue.text: One who was, but didn't remain, mean ogre, 'cos transformed

definitions.text: One who was, but didn't remain, mean

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters of these two words, ignoring the apostrophe, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A miser who reformed, an ogre changed for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebenezer Scrooge in Dickens's A Christmas Carol is a miser who is reformed by the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser was famously tight-fisted until his Christmas Eve visitations changed him.

clue.text: Remove from one part or another in famous theatre you started

indicators.text: from one part or another in
indicators.note: the answer can be taken from either of two places in the words that follow

parts.note: the answer lies across famous and theatre, and again across you and started

explanation.surface: Being thrown out of a famous theatre that you founded.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is hidden twice: once spanning 'famous theatre' and once spanning 'you started', which is what 'one part or another' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to eject or expel someone from a position or place.

clue.text: Gathered up treasure, including ring, in stall

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: people who met have gathered together

indicators.note: the word for treasure takes the ring shape inside it

parts.note: prise is an old spelling of prize, to value highly
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone collecting a hoard, ring and all, at a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a noun for a market booth, but it is the verb meaning to play for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay or evade a decision to gain time, which is what stalling means.

clue.text: Temperature inside hooked fish, very cold

indicators.note: the temperature letter goes within the word for the fish

parts.note: a fish that bites the bait is a biter, and so is hooked

explanation.surface: An angler's thermometer reading: a hooked fish in icy water.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter wind or bitter weather is piercingly cold.

clue.text: Assistants concealing small communications not intended for everyone

indicators.note: the helpers hide the small letter within themselves

parts.note: aides are helpers or assistants

explanation.surface: Assistants hiding brief messages meant only for some.
explanation.definitionFit: In a play, remarks spoken so only the audience hears are private remarks not meant for the other characters.

clue.text: One centigrade? That's right — or even more freezing

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
C is the standard abbreviation for centigrade, or Celsius
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A weather report: one degree centigrade, or colder still.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of icy describes something colder, more frozen.

clue.text: See 11
Spirit associated with seasonal offering that disturbed 4

definitions.meaning: a ghost tied to a gift given at the festive season
4 is Dickens's reformed miser, visited by three spirits in his festive novella

explanation.surface: A ghostly gift-bringer who troubled the reformed miser.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Christmas Carol, Scrooge is visited by three spirits; the second represents the present-day festive season, which doubles as a seasonal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: The second of the three Dickens apparitions is named for the current holiday, a phrase that also means a festive gift.

clue.text: Good antique that's given to person coming in first

definitions.text: that's given to person coming in first

parts.note: something antique is old

explanation.surface: A good antique handed to whoever arrives first.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition also nods to the theme: this was one of the Magi's gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The winner of a race or competition receives the top medal, made of this metal.

clue.text: Are you and I, speaking common sense, causing harm?

indicators.note: said out loud, the two words come out as two letters

parts.note: said aloud the two words sound like the letter names R and U
taken as written
nous is a British word for practical good sense

explanation.surface: A pointed question whether you and I are talking sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'are you' sounds like the letters R and U, as in text-speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous brings disaster or destruction, so it does great damage.

clue.text: Manager who made extra provision for visitors, using popular new defender

definitions.text: Manager who made extra provision for visitors

parts.note: something in is fashionable
a goalkeeper defends the goal

explanation.surface: A football manager bringing in a new popular goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the Nativity, where the innkeeper with no room offered the stable instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord who runs a hostelry manages lodging for travellers, and in the Nativity story found extra space.

clue.text: Lists of competitors making appearances on stage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the people entered in a contest
second meaning: actors' entrances on stage

explanation.surface: A theatre programme listing the performers as they come on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the field of contestants in a race and the act of coming onto a stage.

clue.text: Father or husband as Hemingway's main character?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal phrase for one's dad or one's spouse
second meaning: the fisherman of ... and the Sea, main being the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is an old word for the sea, so the main character is the one in the title with the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a father or a husband, and it is the hero of Hemingway's fishing novella.

clue.text: Most affectionate female doesn't, however upset

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A loving woman who still won't, however upset she is.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of fond describes the person who is most loving.

clue.text: So-called priest producing articles in French

indicators.note: the articles sit inside the abbreviation for French

parts.note: a and the are the English indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A priest turning out pieces written in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic priests are addressed by this title, so a priest is one so called.

clue.text: Picture hard time going North for star's followers

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading the pieces upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: a picture is an image; the clue gives no signal for the letter swap the answer needs
H is the pencil grade for hard

explanation.surface: Imagining a tough time heading north while following a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The intended parse is IMAGE + H + T read upwards, but that gives THEGAMI: the M and G come out swapped, a slip by the setter that the blog points out.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men from the East followed the star of Bethlehem to find the infant Jesus.

clue.text: See 11
Like some cards from shop, last I chose

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the words that follow, across their breaks

parts.note: the answer starts with the last letter of shop and ends with the first letter of chose

explanation.surface: Picking a greetings card at the shop, the last one chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit and debit cards are commonly called by the material they are made of.

clue.text: Very little gift finally causing irritation

indicators.note: only the end letter of the word gift is used

parts.note: its final letter is the one taken
an itchy jumper irritates the skin

explanation.surface: A small present that ends up giving someone a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCHY is British informal for tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang word means tiny or minute.

clue.text: Feature of festive celebrations where you'll find the whole family

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the decorated fir set up indoors at Christmas

definitions.text: where you'll find the whole family
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a genealogical chart showing all relatives

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: the whole family appears on a genealogical chart of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated fir stands in homes at Christmas, and a genealogical chart of ancestors has the same name.

clue.text: Totally, I am within lawful maximum when driving

indicators.note: the totally and I am pieces go inside the word for lawful

parts.note: legit is slang for legitimate
all as in completely
the contraction I'm

explanation.surface: A driver insisting they are fully within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: The speed limit or alcohol limit set by law is the most a driver is allowed.

clue.text: Poetically speaking, not a centre spread

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a poetic word for an edge or border
second meaning: British short for margarine

explanation.walkthrough: MARGE is everyday British for margarine, and also an archaic poetic word for margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic edge rather than a middle, and also the shortened name for a butter substitute.

clue.text: Swindler's confession that may be seen on computer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., a fraudster admitting it

definitions.text: that may be seen on computer
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small picture on screen for a program

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word is a cheat owning up, and whole it is the small image clicked on a desktop.

clue.text: Eager to see what happens, after English arrange next pact

indicators.note: the English letter follows from the clue's start and the rearranged words come after it
the words are to be set in a new order, so their letters are reshuffled

parts.note: these two words provide the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to sort out a new deal with the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Being expectant means waiting in hope or anticipation for something to happen.

clue.text: Maiden and prince returned without a fragrant substance

parts.note: M for maiden is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over with no runs

indicators.note: sent back, so the prince's name is read in reverse
the prince loses the letter a

parts.note: Prince Harry, the Duke of Sussex
the letter a itself is what the prince's name loses

explanation.surface: A maiden and a prince coming home without one perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is one of the Magi's three gifts, fitting the puzzle's Christmas theme.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic resin from a shrub was one of the gifts brought to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Source of pleasant scent making fellow get angry after row

indicators.note: the anger word comes after the row word

parts.note: a rank is a line or row, as of soldiers
to incense is to anger

explanation.surface: A man losing his temper after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line here.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic gum resin is burnt for its sweet smell, and was a Magi gift.
